newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks reach new records on U.S. rally.
newsitem.headline: German stocks reach new records on U.S. rally.

text.p: German shares closed around new record highs on Friday, driven higher by the reaction of U.S. financial markets to a new raft of economic data seen further easing fears of U.S. interest rate increases.

The DAX index of 30 German blue-chips finished 25.64 points, or one percent, higher at 2,595.96, while the IBIS index of all-day electronic trade went on breach the 2,600 threshold for the first time, ending 26.46 points up at 2,614.50.
Dealers said that with this psychologically-important barrier crossed, they could not rule out the index making further gains.
"(Futures) trading is very strong and the technicals are there for another five to six point rise," one trader said, adding that it was too early to say whether the index could move past 2,620.
September DAX futures stood 23.5 points up at 2,615 while German December Bund futures were up 52 basis points at 97.75.

The two keys to the advance were the strong rally on Wall Street after U.S. consumer price and retail sales data interpreted as non-inflationary, and the continued strength of the dollar against the mark.
Traders nonetheless noted one possible obstacle to further gains would be any escalation of tensions between the U.S. and Iraq.
Some admitted to being confused by the strength of the move upwards, noting that nothing fundamental had changed since last week.
"It's all sentiment driving this. In such a mood, there is no resistance on the upside anymore," one said.
Several expressed concern that if U.S. monetary authorities, against the growing consensus, did move to increase rates this month, the market fall-out could be extreme.

Chief beneficiaries of the rally included dollar-sensitive stocks BASF AG up 84 pfennigs on IBIS at 46.44 marks, Schering AG up 1.45 marks at 113.45, and Daimler-Benz AG up 92 pfennigs at 82.73 marks.
These three stocks were mentioned specifically in a study by Germany's Berenberg Bank as worth consideration on a long-term basis with the dollar trading above 1.50 marks.
